solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Trademark gags in a humorous conversation (8)

indicatorNotes.gags: a gag is stuffed in the mouth, so BADGE holds the words

blocks.note: a badge is a trademark, a distinguishing sign
taken as written

annotation.surface: A company's logo is making jokes during a funny chat.
annotation.walkthrough: "Gags" reads as jokes, which suits a humorous conversation; here it is the verb, BADGE stopping up "in a".
annotation.definitionFit: Badinage is light, playful banter.

entries.clue: Heather last seen in tavern opening a second drink (9)

indicatorNotes.last seen in: only the final letter of tavern is seen
indicatorNotes.opening: the pieces open up A MO and go inside

blocks.note: a mo = a second, a moment
Erica is the botanical name for heather
the last letter of tavern

annotation.surface: A woman called Heather is spotted in a pub starting her second drink.
annotation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a drinker's name; it is the plant, ERICA. ERICA plus N go inside A MO.
annotation.definitionFit: An americano is espresso topped up with hot water.

indicatorNotes.novel: novel = new, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: Someone is passionately working on a book manuscript.
annotation.walkthrough: "Novel" wants to be the book being edited; it is the anagram indicator, and "editing" is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Ignited means set alight, a plain synonym for burning.

entries.clue: Cold Indian vegetable with trace of fat (5)

indicatorNotes.trace of: only a trace, the first letter, of fat is used

blocks.note: aloo is potato in Indian cooking
first letter of fat

annotation.surface: A chilled curry side dish with a little fat in it.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cold" sits by the food as a temperature; it is the definition, meaning distant in manner.
annotation.definitionFit: A cold, aloof person keeps others at a distance.

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits inside the following words

blocks.note: thE ATtic

annotation.surface: Storing something up in the loft.
annotation.walkthrough: "Put away" suggests storage in the attic; it is the informal sense of eating heartily.
annotation.definitionFit: Put away is informal for consuming food heartily.

blocks.note: the United Kingdom
to delay is to wait

annotation.surface: A report on the nation mirrors its postponements.
annotation.walkthrough: "State of country" reads as one phrase, a nation's condition; State alone is the definition, a Gulf state.
annotation.definitionFit: Kuwait is a sovereign state on the Persian Gulf.

blocks.note: to keep someone is to pay their way
a yuppy is a young urban professional with money

annotation.surface: A rich young sponsor bankrolls a gifted footballer.
annotation.walkthrough: Keepy-uppy is the skill of keeping a football off the ground with feet, knees and head.
annotation.definitionFit: Keepy-uppy is a trick of ball control, a footballing talent.

blocks.note: William, leader of the Scots against Edward I in the 1290s
split the answer in two: squash is played off a wall, and a champion is an ace

annotation.surface: A Scottish sporting hero who wins at squash.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading as a pun: a squash champion is an ace at the wall.
annotation.definitionFit: William Wallace is Scotland's great medieval patriot, and a squash ace is a wall ace.

entries.clue: Where little intelligence is to be found, eh? (5)

blocks.note: where something is to be found: in
a nit is a person of little intelligence
completes the phrase, so Where reads as a place: in

annotation.surface: A sneer at some place lacking brains, with a questioning tag.
annotation.walkthrough: The front half reads as a jibe at someone dim, but it is a place description in two parts. Innit is British street slang for "isn't it?".
annotation.definitionFit: Innit is a slang question tag, used much like "eh?".

indicatorNotes.within: within means inside, so R is placed inside the wetland word

blocks.note: a fen is marshy land
R = right

annotation.surface: A plant growing properly in a marsh.
annotation.walkthrough: Blocks are listed around the insertion: FEN is split to hold R.
annotation.definitionFit: Ferns are the classic flowerless green plants, a definition by example.

entries.clue: As eyelids may be when about to conk out? (2,3,5)

blocks.note: taken literally: eyelids opening and shutting
the idiom for a machine working fitfully and near failure

annotation.surface: Heavy eyelids flicker as someone is about to nod off.
annotation.walkthrough: "Conk out" suggests falling asleep, which suits the eyelids; it means a machine breaking down.
annotation.definitionFit: A gadget on the blink works only fitfully and is about to fail.

entries.clue: Even money in Liverpool’s banks capped? (5-5)

indicatorNotes.banks: a river's banks are its edges, so the outer letters

blocks.note: the outer letters of Liverpool are L and L, and L is the Roman numeral for fifty
hints that the Ls are capitals, as Roman numerals are written

annotation.surface: A bet at evens on whether Liverpool's riverbanks are overtopped.
annotation.walkthrough: Liverpool's banks sound like the Mersey's, but here they are the word's edges. Each L then has to be read as a number, not a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Fifty-fifty odds are even, an equal chance either way.

blocks.note: felt = thought, considered
a tip is a piece of advice

annotation.surface: Careful guidance offered to an author.
annotation.walkthrough: "Writer" suggests an author receiving advice; it is a pen.
annotation.definitionFit: A felt tip is a pen, something that writes.

entries.clue: Worried about pole, stake taken up? (4)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so ATE is wrapped round the pole

blocks.note: ate = worried, as in "what's eating you?"
N = north pole

annotation.surface: Someone fretting over a post that has been pulled out of the ground.
annotation.walkthrough: "Pole" and "stake" look like a pair of posts; the stake is money, and the pole is N.
annotation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake a poker player puts up before the deal.

entries.clue: Red, sensual dresses I had sent back (8)

indicatorNotes.dresses: CARNAL clothes DI, wrapping round it
indicatorNotes.sent back: something sent back returns the way it came, so I'D is read in reverse

blocks.note: carnal = of the flesh, sensual
I'd is short for I had

annotation.surface: Someone in racy red clothing, whose own outfit was returned.
annotation.walkthrough: "Dresses" reads as garments; it is the verb, CARNAL wrapping DI.
annotation.definitionFit: Cardinal is a deep scarlet, the colour of a cardinal's robes.

entries.clue: Reporter, hack originally into contemporary music? (9)

indicatorNotes.originally: the original, first, letter of hack
indicatorNotes.into: into means going inside, so the letter is put inside the music phrase

blocks.note: a new sound = contemporary music
first letter of hack

annotation.surface: A journalist who was a hack at first moves into writing about the latest music.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hack" looks like a second word for the reporter; only its first letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: A newshound is a keen reporter, always sniffing out stories.

blocks.note: kind of = rather, fairly, as in "kind of good"
prepossessing = attractive

annotation.definitionNote: "Kind of" is an adverbial phrase, so PRETTY is read here as an adverb
annotation.walkthrough: "Kind of" looks like the start of a phrase; it stands alone as the adverb.
annotation.definitionFit: Pretty means both fairly (kind of) and attractive (prepossessing).

entries.clue: Orangey red mist can start to envelop downs (9)

indicatorNotes.start to: the start of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.downs: downs = swallows, so TINE takes ANGER inside

blocks.note: a tin is a can
first letter of envelop
red mist is a sudden fit of anger

annotation.surface: A reddish haze and a can, with talk of envelopes and hills.
annotation.walkthrough: "Red" looks like part of the colour definition; it belongs with "mist" as ANGER. "Envelop" is also a decoy container word: only its first letter is used, and "downs" does the swallowing.
annotation.definitionFit: Tangerine is a deep orange colour, so orangey.

blocks.note: to bob is to bow, a quick bend
a wow is a hit, a big success

annotation.surface: A boxer ducks and throws a punch.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a fight; the boxer is the dog breed, and bow-wow is a child's word for a dog. The question mark flags a boxer as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A bow-wow is a dog in baby talk, and a boxer is a breed of dog.

indicatorNotes.beneath: in a down clue, CHIT sits below WAT

blocks.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
a chit is a short note

annotation.surface: A warning shouted about a note found under a temple, near a cave.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cave" looks like a hollow in a hill; it is Latin for "beware", school slang shouted as a lookout's warning.
annotation.definitionFit: Cave! (Latin, beware) was the schoolboy's cry of "watch it!".

blocks.note: to try a case is to judge it
to smart is to sting

annotation.surface: A sharp judge setting up a meeting.
annotation.walkthrough: "Smart" reads as well dressed or clever; it is the verb, to hurt.
annotation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret lovers' meeting, so trysting fits arranging one.

entries.clue: Mouth mostly holds long, breathing apparatus (7)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of TRAP, dropping its last letter
indicatorNotes.holds: holds means has inside, so TRA keeps ACHE within it

blocks.note: TRAP, slang for mouth, less its last letter
to long for is to ache for

annotation.surface: An open mouth drawing in a long breath.
annotation.walkthrough: "Long" reads as an adjective; it is the verb, to yearn.
annotation.definitionFit: The windpipe carries air to the lungs, part of the breathing apparatus.

indicatorNotes.Laid-back: laid back, so the letters run the other way
indicatorNotes.scrubbing back: the back, last letter, of TITAN is scrubbed out

blocks.note: TITAN, a giant, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A relaxed giant scrubbing someone's back: are they busy?
annotation.walkthrough: "Laid-back" and "busy" look like opposites describing the giant; one reverses the letters and the other is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone at it is hard at work, busy.

entries.clue: Significant part of Russia thawing was seen periodically (5)

indicatorNotes.seen periodically: only every other letter is seen

blocks.note: ThAwInG wAs: letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9

annotation.surface: A big region of Russia melting was spotted from time to time.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface about thawing is apt: the taiga is the snowy conifer forest of Siberia.
annotation.definitionFit: The taiga, the vast subarctic forest, covers much of Russia.

entries.clue: Barely inept, they had failed — as half-witted ex-husband and father-in-law? (10)

indicatorNotes.Barely: stripped bare of its outer letters
indicatorNotes.failed: the letters fail to hold their order

blocks.note: inept without its outer letters
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A foolish ex-husband and a father-in-law, both inept, have both failed.
annotation.walkthrough: "Half-witted" seems to insult the relatives; the words half-witted, ex-husband and father-in-law are all written with hyphens.
annotation.definitionFit: Each of the three words is spelt with a hyphen, so each is hyphenated.

entries.clue: Forward almost missing end of season (5)

blocks.note: nearly = almost
last letter of season, removed

annotation.surface: A footballer nearly out for the rest of the season.
annotation.walkthrough: "Forward" looks like a football position; it means ahead of time, as a forward spring.
annotation.definitionFit: Forward can mean early, as with advanced growth or a forward season.

blocks.note: high = elated
a jumper is a sweater, a top

annotation.surface: A thrilled leading athlete.
annotation.walkthrough: "Top" reads as best; it is a garment, a jumper being a British sweater.
annotation.definitionFit: High jump is a track-and-field event, so its competitor is an athlete.

entries.clue: Pickles are horrid, first of all — yuck! (3)

indicatorNotes.first of all: the first letter of each word

blocks.note: Pickles Are Horrid

annotation.surface: Someone who hates pickles says so, with disgust.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is exactly the sort of thing you would say "pah!" about.
annotation.definitionFit: Pah is an exclamation of disgust, like yuck.

indicatorNotes.Reporter’s: a reporter speaks on air, so this is the word as heard

blocks.note: hale = robust, as in hale and hearty

annotation.surface: A news reporter's hearty hello.
annotation.walkthrough: "Reporter" looks like a journalist; here it only signals a word said out loud.
annotation.definitionFit: Hail is an old salutation, a synonym for greeting.

indicatorNotes.crackers: crackers = crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

annotation.surface: Salty biscuits stayed crisp.
annotation.walkthrough: "Crackers" is a biscuit in the surface; it is the adjective, mad.
annotation.definitionFit: Food that lasted stayed fresh and fit to eat.

blocks.note: a machine for tossing and drying cut grass
a wild, swinging punch

annotation.surface: A tractor is a great success.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense comes from the wide swing of a scythe at haymaking.
annotation.definitionFit: Haymaker names both the farm machine and a big punch.
